newsitem.title: USA: GM to shake up Delco Electronics unit - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: GM to shake up Delco Electronics unit - WSJ.

text.p: General Motors Corp is expected to announce a shake-up at its Delco Electronics automotive unit and disclose the unit's profit to be lower than expected, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday.

The newspaper also said Gary Dickinson, the unit's president and chief executive officer, would retire early for personal reasons. Dickson, who is also executive vice president of the GM Hughes Electronics Corp unit, would be succeeded by someone from inside GM, it added.
The newspaper said GM would reveal how Delco's margins were being squeezed, largely by GM's own automotive operations in North America.
It said plans to invest in personnel changes, plant and equipment during the next 18-24 months had also affected margins. The rate of return was still expected to be in double digits, it added.
Industry analysts had been projecting Delco to produce a 13-percent operating profit margin.
Delco makes air-bag electronics, anti-lock brake controls and security systems, among other things.
